correctness.rationale: The graph-to-distance equivalence is exact for every binary source, not an approximation. Any second source has a nonempty difference set D of size exactly 2 or 4; these are exactly a two-vertex exact transversal or an active-vertex set of size ≤4. The exhaustive classification of four-edge graphs by components and bipartitions and independent count of each labeled graph type establish the all-n formula. Two distinct complete finite implementations give the same counts through n=9 (including all quadruples at each n). Finite experiments only corroborate the general combinatorial proof.

originality.rationale: Closest full primary sources were compared on mathematical implication, not title similarity. Wang–Yaakobi–Zhang Theorem 10 yields disjoint-triple sufficiency, covering three of the four infinite forest families but not triangle plus disjoint edge or the length-five star; the latter is uniquely decodable in exact-two channel despite majority failure. Papadopoulou et al. calculate worst-case read threshold and decoder behaviour, not the four-read motif taxonomy or its exact all-n count. Junnila et al. give a generic algorithm for intersections of arbitrary Hamming balls, which does not state closed shell-singleton motif classes or count. Semantic mathematical-record searches and published mathematics literature claims revealed no corresponding theorem. An older equivalent combinatorial graph classification could remain unindexed.
residual_risks: The general formula for arbitrary Hamming-ball intersections can be specialized through inclusion–exclusion and might conceal this classification in an unrecognized representation.

value.rationale: This is a naturally motivated first nontrivial complete four-read local reconstruction classification in a current exact-weight-substitution channel. It resolves all binary error-two, four-distinct-read instances, gives closed counts for each length, and isolates 10*C(n,5) genuinely four-read triangle-plus-edge patterns, plus a length-five 5-star exception where optimal unique decoding succeeds despite wrong simple majority. Neither a worst-case threshold nor three-read sufficient conditions supply the irreducible types. General higher-error or higher-read cases are not claimed.
